content.value_statement: Biology teams need reproducible data systems that connect datasets, metadata, workflows, and ontology terms. This skill guides LaminDB setup, curation, querying, lineage tracking, and integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains LaminDB concepts including artifacts, records, transforms, runs, features, and collections.
Guides biological dataset registration, metadata annotation, validation, and ontology standardization.
Provides query patterns for artifacts, feature filters, collections, and large dataset streaming.
Covers setup choices for local SQLite, cloud storage, PostgreSQL, cache settings, and team deployments.
Describes integrations with workflow managers, MLOps tools, cloud storage, and visualization systems.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run LaminDB commands by itself.
It does not replace the official LaminDB documentation for version-specific API changes.
It cannot verify private datasets, cloud permissions, or database connectivity without user-provided context.
It does not provide clinical, regulatory, or biosafety approval for research workflows.

use_cases.title: Curate single-cell datasets
use_cases.description: Plan registration, metadata validation, ontology mapping, and lineage tracking for scRNA-seq or spatial datasets.

use_cases.title: Design research data infrastructure
use_cases.description: Compare local, cloud, and production deployment patterns for storage, databases, cache, and team access.

use_cases.title: Connect model experiments to data
use_cases.description: Link W&B, MLflow, workflow managers, and versioned biological artifacts through shared provenance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a LaminDB project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a local LaminDB instance for a new biology project. Explain the decisions I need to make.

prompt_templates.title: Plan dataset curation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LaminDB curation plan for my dataset. I have these metadata fields and these ontology requirements: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Build queryable lineage
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to structure LaminDB artifacts, features, collections, and lineage tracking for this analysis workflow: [workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Review production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my LaminDB deployment plan for cloud storage, PostgreSQL, cache settings, user access, and workflow integrations: [plan].

output_examples.input: I need to organize scRNA-seq batches and query by tissue and treatment.
output_examples.output: A practical data model with artifact keys, typed metadata features, ontology-backed tissue terms, and query steps before loading large files.

output_examples.input: My cell type labels contain synonyms and invalid names.
output_examples.output: A curation workflow that standardizes labels, separates invalid terms, maps accepted terms to Bionty records, and records validation decisions.

output_examples.input: We want to move from a local instance to a shared cloud deployment.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering storage choice, database choice, credential handling, cache location, backup planning, and team access boundaries.

best_practices: Start tracking before each analysis so outputs keep clear lineage.
Validate metadata and ontology terms before downstream analysis.
Query metadata first, then load only the datasets you need.
anti_patterns: Running analyses before tracking starts, which leaves lineage incomplete.
Duplicating datasets under new keys instead of using versioning.
Loading large files before narrowing results with metadata queries.

faq.question: What is LaminDB used for?
faq.answer: LaminDB manages biological datasets with metadata, lineage, validation, and query support for reproducible research.

faq.question: Does this skill execute LaminDB commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Which data types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers DataFrames, AnnData, MuData, SpatialData, TileDB-SOMA, Parquet, CSV, and related biological artifacts.

faq.question: Can it help with biological ontologies?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains validation and standardization with Bionty for genes, cell types, tissues, diseases, and related terms.

faq.question: Can it support cloud deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes local SQLite, cloud storage, PostgreSQL, cache configuration, and team deployment patterns.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for official documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as task-focused guidance and confirm version-specific details in the official LaminDB documentation.
